Params: A vehicle rumbles across open country, jolting along fractured concrete roads flanked by the burned-out, collapsed towers of the Golden Age.
Even now, the air feels thick with the ghost of gunsmoke rising from those gray mounds of rubble.
Satisfied that there are no enemies outside, Leia turns her attention back to the interior of the vehicle.
It is a transport vehicle borrowed from the rear base. Issarius is at the wheel, while Leia has been stationed alongside Sylph in the back to keep watch over Jorge.
Upon meeting Jorge, Leia was briefed by Issarius on their next move: Jorge would guide them to the last place he met with the Ascendant in secret.
Issarius believed that they would find something tied to the Ascendant in that location.
...Sylph, can I ask Mr. Jorge something?
Drop the "Mr." He's nothing but a traitor now.
Sylph's voice is cold as steel, without a trace of warmth in it.
Um... Jorge, sir, did you really betray us? Are you actually working with the Ascendant?
A silence settles over the cabin. After a long moment, Jorge slowly lifts his head and answers, his voice rough and hoarse.
Yes, I betrayed Babylonia, but... I never worked with the Ascendant willingly. I was coerced.
From the moment Sylph laid eyes on Jorge, she had become a completely different person. This must be how the Purifying Force operates, Leia thinks to herself.
Yeah... Whatever the circumstances, I did betray Babylonia.
So what exactly did you do with the Ascendant... and who is this Ascendant, anyway?

That's exactly what we're here to find out, Jorge. We paused the questioning earlier because your M.I.N.D. was unstable, but you're stable now. So let's continue... Tell us everything about you and the Ascendant.
Jorge draws a deep breath and gives a slow, heavy nod.
My name is Jorge. I was born here in the TEC, and I joined the military when I was young to get by. That's how I became a soldier.
And so the years passed, until the World Government flagged my Tantalum affinity during the Great Evacuation. I accepted the procedure and became a Construct.
But the early operations were far from perfect, and the batch I was in was one of the worse ones. This frame has been a mess of problems ever since.
After being damaged in the field, command decided that I was no longer fit for frontline combat, so they pulled me back and reassigned me to the Support Force.
After that, I spent my time managing logistics and supply lines, until eventually, command turned its attention back to the Atlantic region.
They issued me transfer orders and sent me back here to oversee supply management for the area.
And it was there, as I was wandering at those strange yet familiar ruins, that the Ascendant found me.
Jorge falls silent. A flicker of cold dread crosses his eyes.
Amazigh... I've never heard that name before.
I don't know if it's her real name, but that's what she called herself.
Hm... could it have been another Ascendant posing as her?
Unlikely. We had Jorge go through every Ascendant on record, and he confirmed Amazigh wasn't among them.
So that's why they said it could be a new Ascendant faction at the briefing...
Sylph does not give Leia's musing much thought. She steers the conversation back on track, her gaze cutting sharply toward Jorge from beneath her hood.
What does Amazigh want? What did she ask of you?
She wants me to keep up the lie "we" spun back during the Great Evacuation.
Keep up the lie... What did you do during the Great Evacuation? And who exactly is this "we"?
I colluded with certain high-ranking officers in the warzone. Together, we falsified shipping routes across the entire Atlantic and built a network of ghost warehouses that existed only on paper.
As the truth leaves his lips, Jorge's voice breaks, as though the confession itself is a form of penance.
Falsifying routes and warehouses that never existed in the first place... for what?
Diverting wartime supplies, then selling them off... You were finding ways to profit from the chaos, weren't you?
Diverting supplies and selling them off... Wait, wasn't there a shortage back then? Wasn't that whole period incredibly desperate?
That hardship was only ever felt by some.
The outbreak didn't destroy humanity overnight. Much of the vast industrial infrastructure left behind by the Golden Age continued to function.
Then why have I heard people say they didn't have enough food or ammunition back then...?
Because people like Jorge hoarded the supplies and sold them... to those who had nothing, as you mentioned, and to the underground resistance groups.
The world was falling apart... so why would they still do something like that?
As long as civilization exists, capital is the only thing that matters. Those officials clawed their way to the top with exactly that belief.
So even the Great Evacuation was nothing more than a golden opportunity to them.
Corruption was everywhere back then... Some of it was eventually exposed and brought to justice. The rest was buried.
And those falsified routes I just described... were among the ones that got buried.
Not buried... covered up. Some of the officials who were in on it are still alive aboard Babylonia, aren't they?
...The lies are clear enough, but why does Amazigh need these fabricated routes and warehouses?
Babylonia's systems are airtight and heavily monitored nowadays. The moment anyone tries to activate those fabricated routes, they'd be flagged instantly.
That's what puzzles Leia the most. Even if the system somehow missed it, someone would notice immediately the moment anyone actually used those roads or warehouses.
At that, Jorge looks at the fields outside and shakes his head.
So the Ascendant made all of them real.
Without anyone noticing, she took every last one of those fabricated facilities and roads and made them real.
While I was still reeling from the shock, she ordered me to have Babylonia use the route as normal and keep them running like legitimate rear-line logistics.
The road we're driving on right now, and... that burned warehouse ahead—
All of them are created by the Ascendant.
The words have barely left his mouth when the vehicle comes to a smooth stop.

Through the window, the collapsed ruins come into view. What was once a military warehouse is now utterly destroyed, leaving behind nothing but warped steel beams on a scorched and blackened wasteland.
Stepping out of the vehicle after Issarius, Leia is hit by the sharp, acrid air immediately. The smell of chemical burn is tangled with gunpowder and ash, filling the whole area.
Military warehouses store all kinds of things, and judging by the smell... someone torched the place. Jorge, this is the last place you saw the Ascendant, correct?
There's nothing left, just as I feared... Caro...
Leia and the others spin around to find Jorge collapsed against the ruins of the warehouse, desperately clawing through the concrete, as if he is trying to dig something out from underneath.
Sorry, he just ran straight for it the moment he got out. I couldn't stop him.
Mr. Jorge... what are you doing?
Caro... I see. Your child is buried under there, is that right?
Unlike Sylph and Leia, Issarius seems to have cut straight to the heart of what Jorge is doing.
Issarius, what child are you talking about?
I pulled Jorge's file and found that he adopted a number of children just before he boarded Babylonia.
One of them became a Construct, citing "admiration for her father" as her reason. That child's name... was Caro.
Recently, she filed for temporary leave, stating that she wanted to visit her adoptive father. And her scheduled check-in went dark yesterday.
Those words are the last straw. Jorge finally breaks.
His hands go still against the rubble, his shoulders heaving, his voice filled with grief and rage.
I did everything... everything to keep them safe, to give them a life away from all of this... so why... why did it end up like this...?
Wait, you said "one of them." Don't tell me all of Jorge's adopted children are on Babylonia?
Jorge's fingers close around a chunk of concrete, his body trembling as he finally lets go of the last secret he has kept buried.
When I helped those officials falsify the routes and rig the system, it was never about what I'd get out of it.
You should know: spots on Babylonia are limited, but not set. There's room up there, and somewhere in the chain, hidden from plain sight, Babylonia has always allowed a little overflow.
To save those children, I agreed to their terms and carried out the corrupted scheme they'd designed.
In the end, they got what they wanted, and I got the children onto Babylonia, and took them in as my own... including Caro.
Those officials could really pull that off? Back when I was on the surface, I heard people were fighting tooth and nail just for a single spot on Babylonia...

In those chaotic times, spots being transferred, bought, sold, or even handed out behind closed doors wasn't unheard of. And people with the right connections always had reserved allocations to begin with.
Without warning, Sylph lunges forward and grabs Jorge by the collar, hauling him up off the ruins.
To save those children, you took up spots that belonged to someone else, maybe even stealing their spots outright.
...Do you have any idea how many people who could have been saved died because of what you did?! How many were left behind in these ruins forever?!
Hoisted up, Jorge struggles to breathe, but he makes no move to resist. Through the pain, he forces the words out.
Cough... I have nightmares every night. Strangers... faces I've never seen... they'd drag me down into hell.
But it was the only way... I was the only one who could save them!
Just as Sylph moves to tighten her grip, Issarius cuts in with the order. Reluctantly, she lets Jorge go.
...I helped Amazigh because she found out about the children. What I did to falsify those routes was the leverage she had over me.
To keep it all buried, to keep Caro and the others from being branded as a criminal's children, I had no choice but to play along and keep her false logistics network running.
But it all ended yesterday. Everything I did back then finally caught up with me.
So Caro really is buried here?
Yes... This warehouse was where I met Amazigh for the last time. Where we made the exchange.
And in the middle of it, Caro walked in. She saw everything.
